name: KEI Industries Ltd.
business_summary: Indian manufacturer of power cables (EHV up to 400 kV, HT, LT), house wires, control/instrumentation cables and stainless-steel wire, plus a small EPC arm. Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 3,776 cr (+38.5%), EBITDA margin 9.97%, PAT Rs 262 cr; wire & cable order book Rs 4,927 cr (Rs 991 cr exports, ~50% US). Debt-free with Rs 698 cr cash. Guides 25%+ FY27 revenue growth, 20% CAGR over 3-4 years and 11-12% EBITDA margin as Sanand EHV Phase 2 ramps (Mar 2027). Stock is -27% in 3 months on a Q2 margin miss and UltraTech's Sept entry into cables.

revenue_mix.segment: Stainless steel wire, EPC and others

exposures.mechanism: UltraTech (Aditya Birla) launched Ultravolt W&C on 3 Sep 2026 with Rs 1,800 cr initial capex; Nuvama expects aggressive pricing/channel investment -> margin pressure and interim de-rating. +1 = incumbent W&C gross margin -100 bp industry-wide (house wires/LT cables first, EHV least exposed). KEI OPM ~10-11%: -100 bp group-wide = EBITDA -9%; only ~60% of revenue (LT/HT/house wires) is contested near term, plus modest share-loss risk -> EBITDA ~-6%; EV/MCap 0.98; persistence 0.5 (structural but fades as incumbents respond) -> ~-3, plus de-rating risk -> central -5. Partly priced: W&C stocks fell up to 16% in a week and KEI -27% in 3m.

evidence.note: KEI -8% on the day; Nuvama: aggressive pricing and channel investment could cause interim de-rating

exposures.mechanism: EHV/HT cables for transmission, substations, renewable evacuation and metros; Sanand EHV Phase 2 (commissioning ~Mar 2027) adds Rs 1,500-1,700 cr revenue potential. +1 = grid build-out 10% above plan -> EHV/HT volumes +6% (~40% of revenue) -> +2.4% revenue; operating leverage 1.5x -> EBITDA +3.6%; EV/MCap 0.98; persistence 1.0 x 0.8 (competition) -> ~+3; add multiple support -> +4.

evidence.note: EHV capacity expansion at Sanand, Phase 2 by March 2027; 20% revenue CAGR guided 3-4 yrs

exposures.mechanism: Utilities, discoms, railways/metro, roads and water projects take ~30% of demand. +10% government capex -> +3% volumes -> +3% revenue; fixed-cost leverage 1.6x -> EBITDA +4.8%; EV/MCap 0.98; persistence 0.5 -> +2.3; plus growth-multiple support -> ~+3.

evidence.note: Domestic wire & cable sales +46% y/y in Q2 FY27; management guides 25%+ revenue growth FY27

exposures.mechanism: Industrial, data-centre, real-estate and RE-developer demand ~35% of volume. +10% private capex -> +3.5% volumes -> EBITDA +5% at leverage 1.4x; EV/MCap 0.98 x persistence 0.5 -> ~+2.4.

evidence.note: Order book Rs 4,927 cr incl. Rs 991 cr exports

exposures.mechanism: Data-centre power cabling (LT/HT, building wire) was a stated driver of Ultravolt's entry and of incumbents' growth. +1 = data-centre capex 20% above plan -> cable demand ~+1.5% of KEI revenue; EBITDA +2.5%; persistence 1.0 x EV/MCap 0.98 x 0.8 -> ~+2.

evidence.note: Headline via Google News: Aditya Birla Group enters wires, cables biz with Rs 1,800-crore investment amid data centre boom (page not fetched)

exposures.mechanism: Copper is ~55% of cost (estimate; RM ~88% of costs). Pricing is LME-linked daily for LT/house wires and via price-variation clauses for HT/EHV, so a +10% move is largely passed through, giving inventory gains short term (positive) but higher working capital and some demand deferral. Q2 FY27 gross margin fell y/y from 'inventory valuation impacts', i.e. the inventory effect is real and can reverse. Net: +10% copper -> inventory gain ~1% of revenue for 1 quarter -> EBITDA +9% on a quarter, persistence 0.1 -> +0.9; demand deferral offsets -> +0.8. Empirical +0.92 (t +0.9) agrees.

evidence.note: Gross margin declined y/y on inventory valuation impacts and EPC losses

exposures.mechanism: House wires and LT cables ~25-30% of revenue (estimate). +10% residential sales -> +4% in that segment -> +1.1% revenue -> EBITDA +1.8%; x0.98 x persistence 0.5 -> ~+0.9, plus sentiment -> +1.2.

evidence.note: Pack: KEI sales TTM Rs 13,393 cr, +25%

exposures.mechanism: Exports ~12% of revenue (US ~50% of Rs 991 cr export order book), priced in USD; copper is LME-linked so import cost passes through. +3% USD/INR -> +0.36% revenue at ~100% margin -> EBITDA +3%; hedging halves it; x0.98 x persistence 0.5 -> ~+0.6 (rounded).

evidence.note: Export order book Rs 991 cr, ~50% from the US

exposures.mechanism: Almost debt-free (cash Rs 698 cr; interest Rs 70 cr TTM vs EBITDA Rs 1,474 cr) so the earnings channel is small; main channel is the multiple (37x trailing) and customers' (builders, EPC) funding cost. +25 bp -> ~-1.2.

evidence.note: Debt-free, cash and bank Rs 698 cr

exposures.mechanism: US is ~6% of revenue (half of ~12% exports, estimate) at above-average margin. +10 pp tariff -> ~20% volume loss on that slice -> -1.2% revenue at ~15% margin -> EBITDA -1.6%; x0.98 x persistence 0.5 -> ~-0.8.

evidence.note: ~50% of export orders from the US

exposures.mechanism: Empirical +2.25 per +5% S&P (t +2.1) with market beta 1.45; most of this is beta, not a causal link (US exposure is only ~6% of revenue), so shrunk to ~+1.0 for the residual.
